newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums slump on Nov IPE fitters.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums slump on Nov IPE fitters.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums slid by over $2 on Tuesday on good Russian supply and fears that the main long might not lift all its November IPE contract obligations.
Benchmark Dec IPE futures ended down $2 at $217 a tonne with heavy selling by a broking house on behalf of a trade customer.
"It sounds like there could be a lot of heating oil hanging over the market," a trader said.
He was referring to a flurry of statements by AIC and Cargill blaming each other for the slow exchange in ARA of about 627,800 tonnes of the record high 865,1000 tonnes November delivery.

AIC, the main short, said Cargill, the main long, had failed to lift a large part of the amount it was due to take in Nov 21-25 and AIC might have to dispense with the oil on "a weak market". Cargill suggests the problem stems from delays by AIC.
Traders said Russian premiums slid $2 to Dec IPE +$2.50 because closure of the U.S. arbitrage left cargoes looking for homes.
Heating oil refinery cargoes were down $2 at Dec IPE +$3. Low sulphur diesel cargoes were easier at Dec IPE +$14/17.
Barge premiums were stable. Heating oil traded at Dec IPE +$2 prompt and +$2.25 for early December fob Rotterdam. Low sulphur diesel was stable at Dec IPE +$10.50/12.50.
